chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who made it upon himself to fast one month in al-Kufah, one month in al-Madinah, and one month in Makkah as expiation for a trial he was tested with. It was ruled that he fasted one month in al-Kufah, then entered al-Madinah and fasted eighteen days there, and did not remain (reside) in al-Jammal. He said: 'He fasts what remains of his obligation when he reaches his hometown.'
ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a vow of fasting in multiple cities if one travels between them?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudence of *Nadhr* (vows) regarding travel, establishing that fasting obligations incurred in one location do not expire merely by entering another city unless the vow specifies residence. The Imam’s ruling emphasizes that the remaining days must be completed in the original city of vow-making, reflecting the Shia principle that the location of the vow's origin dictates the fulfillment site when no specific alternative is mandated. This distinction is crucial for distinguishing between temporary travel (*safar*) and permanent relocation in Islamic legal theory.
